meetings.title: Procurement Review
meetings.summary_text: The procurement review covered the stationery contract, the printer leases and the approval limits. The group agreed to renew the stationery contract with Paper Trail for two years, since it is five percent cheaper and reliable, with Owen confirming the renewal with Joanne and Hannah checking the terms first. The printer leases were extended by the vendor until June at the same price, so that matter is settled. The purchase approval limit without a second quote will rise from two thousand to five thousand dollars from the first of December.

Hannah noted the limit increase should be paired with keeping the register of purchases up to date.

meetings.title: Board Risk Committee Meeting
meetings.summary_text: The risk committee reviewed four items: the top risks register, cyber security, supplier concentration and the budget contingency. The committee added regulatory change as a fourth top risk, and the Fernwood contingency reserve was kept ring-fenced until the November forecast is reviewed. Helen agreed to bring a plan for alternatives to the two most critical supplier services to the next meeting, and Ingrid and Omar agreed to circulate papers for the next audit committee.

meetings.title: Customer Success Retrospective
meetings.summary_text: The Customer Success retrospective reviewed the last quarter, noting improved response times and an 86% satisfaction score alongside onboarding delays caused by a lost trainer. The team linked cancellations to customers who had been inactive for sixty days, and agreed to reach out at forty-five days of inactivity. Actions were assigned for an inactivity report, call script, handover template, sales meeting, follow-up retrospective and a team celebration.

decisions.text: Customers will be contacted at forty-five days of inactivity, before they reach sixty days.
A one-page handover template will be created and agreed with the sales team.

highlights.text: Satisfaction score rose to eighty-six percent and response times improved.
New customers waited more than two weeks for their first training session after a trainer was lost and not backfilled quickly.
The Marlin Point churn review showed most cancelled accounts had not logged in for sixty days before cancelling.
Sales handovers sometimes leave the team unaware of what was promised to customers.

action_items.description: Build the inactivity report and share it
Write the customer call script
Draft the one-page handover template
Set up a meeting with the sales lead
Book the follow-up retrospective
Arrange a celebration of the improved satisfaction score with the team

meetings.title: Security Incident Debrief
meetings.summary_text: The debrief reviewed the Cobalt Reef phishing drill, in which 61 of 400 staff clicked the link and 23 entered credentials, an improvement on the previous drill but still too many. Ninety staff reported the simulated message, and the fastest report came within four minutes, which was seen as a strong result. The team agreed on actions: Dmitri will test a mobile-visible banner for external emails, Beth will draft a reporting reminder for Karim's approval, Karim will report results to the executive team, and the next drill will be scheduled for the middle of next quarter.

decisions.text: The next phishing drill will be planned for the middle of next quarter.
Beth will draft a reminder on reporting suspicious emails, and Karim will approve it.

highlights.text: Most people who clicked were on mobile devices, where the sender address is harder to see.
Nobody was disciplined, so that staff feel safe reporting.

action_items.description: Test the external email banner on mobile and report back
Draft the reminder about reporting suspicious emails and send it to Karim for approval
Report the drill results to the executive team

meetings.title: Sustainability Working Group
meetings.summary_text: The first sustainability working group meeting agreed to remove single-use cups from all office kitchens on 1 March 2027, with reception keeping reusable cups for visitors. The group agreed that Owen will lead refill stations on every floor, with installation targeted for the end of January, and that a quarterly electronic waste collection day will start on 14 February. A four-week waste audit was agreed so that current waste levels can be compared with later results, and the group will meet again in four weeks.
